title: The Adherent Shruber
description: This is a frog-shaped textured brass keychain inspired by the photo above. It was my very first project that I made in jewelry. I still like it a lot, though I realize that I should have been more precise making it at the time. Somehow the branches on either side of the frog do not actually aline.

title: The Fallen Watcher
description:
A bent copper bookmark showing a skeleton staring at a bee nest on a tree. I stamped this one a lot to give it texture. That is how the tree, leaves, beehive, and basically everything looks so detailed. This taught me how to use stamps, and also how to draw most of a skeleton. I spent a long time practicing on drawing a good skull. I also realized the downside of stamps and texture, that it can stretch the metal a lot. This was a gift for my mother, and I had a lot of fun making it.
We were supposed to write a story to get ideas, here is mine:

There is a bee, flying around. To a flower it flys, away from its friends in the hives. Slowly it drifts forward to collect the pollen which it will bring back to make honey. It slowly drones forward with nothing in sight, aimless it moves, no knowledge of below it. Below where he lurks, hidden from sight. Death lurks for those bees who can no longer maintain flight.

title: The Silver Shaker
description: This is a very thick banded silver ring, with lava rock set in prongs. The prongs unfortunately are a bit loose, so the rock shakes when moved. The band was inspired by the horns visible in the final bossfight of Hollow Knight. When setting this ring, I struggled a lot to get the prongs on. This is my fault, because I did not have a good plan from the beginning. Because I was struggling to get even two prongs soldered to the ring, I decided to stop with my two prongs and not risk going for a third. Instead, I cut both of the prongs down the middle so I would effectively have four prongs, so the rock could actually be secure.

title: The Perpetual Witness
description: As part of my first lost wax casting, I made a spider. Although a few limbs did not fully attach, I was able to replace them. I really like how this guy turned out. It was intended to be a charm who watched over me and prevented boredom. That is why it has so many eyes on top of it's head. It is made out of bronze, but I stained it so it is dark. However, I stained it way too much so it looks brown.

title: The Retentive Sundial

images.alt: Sketches and ideas for tree casting

description: As part of my first lost wax casting assignment, I replicated The Persistence of Memory by Salvador Dalí. Making the bark was pretty difficult, but I think it turned out pretty good, if not quite tree-like. I did not think about the numbers on the clock when I had this idea, because making tiny recognizable numbers is hard. This was supposed to be a charm that would help me be more efficient with my time and stop procrastinating. I do not think it has worked.

title: The Lush Ridge
description: I decided to make my sister a birthday gift, and this is what it was. It contains a quartz rock from a trip to Mexico, and the band features a leaf design. It was a bit sloppy, and I wish I had more time to polish it up, but overall it is not a terrible ring. It is actually quite comfortable, because the leaves bend outward making it easy to put on and take off.

title: The Sterling Rabbit
description: I made a small silver cast rabbit for my sister at Christmas. She likes bunnies, so I made one her a lopeared bunny. It is small, but still has large amounts of detail because it was made out of soft wax. I even gave it the texture of fur using a toothpick. I was unable to file off a little piece of scrap metal connected to it's foot, which is visible in the above photo.

title: The Sedentary Liver
description: This is a fairly large silver signet ring depicting one of my dogs, Tucker, asleep. It uses two plates soldered ontop one another to increase the depth and make an image. The back plate was stained with liver of sulfur for better contrast. I polished this a lot so it became extremely reflective. This is one of my favorite pieces.

title: The Coral Bauble

images.alt: Silver signet ring with pink rock

description: For Christmas, I made my mother a silver signet ring with a pink gemstone bezel set on top. Personally, I think this thing looks fantastic. It was one of my first times creating a signet ring and also one of my first times using a bezel setting. However, I was able to use it effetively to create a splendid ring. The stone I set was not round, so I had to cut it and carve it into the correct shape. I then sanded it down and polished it with the few tools I had. It never became shiny, but I also did not have the right tools to make it shiny.

title: The Leaping Polliwog

images.alt: Small silver frog from left view
Small silver frog from right view

description: I always enjoyed tiny statues of creatures. I had the opportunity to make a small thing out of soft wax, so I decided to make a jumping frog. It was difficult, even though it did not turn out as nice as I had hoped it would. Making a statues from soft wax is required me to start over many times, because I might burn too much wax while trying to attach a leg or cut a hole by the tongue.

title: The Crimson Poltroon

images.alt: Large chicken ring with ruby set, front view
Large chicken ring with ruby set, left view
Large chicken ring with ruby set, right view
Large chicken ring with ruby set, side view

description: For my grandmother, I made a silver chicken ring with a ruby in a prong setting. She loves chickens so I made the entire ring into a chicken sitting on your finger. In front and behind the chicken are two roses, because they are my grandmother's favorite flower. Her birthstone is a ruby, so there is a large ruby prong set in the center of the chicken. This was carved out of hard wax and taught me patience. The chicken turned out a little bit too big, so the ring ended up being cluncky and heavy, but it is still nice. I think my favorite part is the roses. They were made out of soft wax and melted onto the ring, and I really love how they look.

title: The Fathomless Ward
description: I wanted to make a special card holder for a MTG commander, so I made this. It works as intended and it is pretty nice. I kind of cheated on the hinges, because instead of using four tubes like I planned, I used only two. This means that it is very unstable. I also just bent the ends up rather than riveting them. However, it is still functional, and even locks in place, which is nice.

title: The Revolving Aureole

images.alt: A spinning ring, in full form
A spinning ring, on the ground

description: I wanted to make this, because I thought it would be epic. I wanted to have something to fidget with in class, because class can be boring, and spinning rings are fun. I was sort of inspired by the time turner from Harry Potter, but I did come up with most of this on my own. I failed to get one pin soldered, so this ring is not perfect. It sort of sounds weird when it spins, and is not great at spinning. This ring is not very polished, but that is not the point of it. It was designed to be fun rather than pretty.

title: The Jingling Chime
description: I wanted to make a bell, so I decided to make this. It ended up nice, and has a clear ring to it. I did not polish the inside, because it would have been very difficult, and I think it looks fine just like this. I really enjoyed making this bell. It was also fun to work on something more technical and linear in style rather than typical artsy jewelry.
